recipe: Declare functions in extern blocks without a body; terminate the declaration with a semicolon instead.
trigger_condition: You are declaring a function inside an extern block.
evidence: Functions within external blocks are declared in the same way as other Rust functions, with the exception that they must not have a body and are instead terminated by a semicolon.

recipe: Use only simple IDENTIFIER or _ for parameter names in extern block functions; do not use patterns.
trigger_condition: You are writing parameter lists for functions declared in an extern block.
evidence: Patterns are not allowed in parameters, only IDENTIFIER or _ may be used.

recipe: Only apply the safe or unsafe qualifier to functions in extern blocks; avoid const, async, or extern qualifiers.
trigger_condition: You are adding qualifiers to a function declared inside an extern block.
evidence: The safe and unsafe function qualifiers are allowed, but other function qualifiers (e.g. const, async, extern) are not.

recipe: Remember that functions in extern blocks are implicitly unsafe unless you explicitly add the safe qualifier.
trigger_condition: You are calling a function declared in an extern block from Rust code.
evidence: A function declared in an extern block is implicitly unsafe unless the safe function qualifier is present.

recipe: Do not use the safe qualifier on a variadic function in an extern block unless you can guarantee it never accesses the variadic arguments.
trigger_condition: You are declaring a variadic function in an extern block and considering whether to mark it safe.
evidence: The safe qualifier should not be used on a function in an extern block unless that function guarantees that it will not access the variadic arguments at all.

recipe: Declare statics in extern blocks without an initialization expression; the value is provided by the linked C code.
trigger_condition: You are declaring a static item inside an extern block.
evidence: Statics within external blocks are declared in the same way as statics outside of external blocks, except that they do not have an expression initializing their value.

recipe: Use the link attribute on extern blocks to specify which native library the compiler should link against.
trigger_condition: You need to tell the compiler which native library to link for items declared in an extern block.
evidence: The link attribute specifies the name of a native library that the compiler should link with for the items within an extern block.

recipe: Always include the name key in the link attribute when you also specify a kind value.
trigger_condition: You are using the link attribute with a kind parameter (e.g. static, framework, raw-dylib).
evidence: The name key must be included if kind is specified.

recipe: In Rust 2024 edition, always write the unsafe keyword before extern in external blocks.
trigger_condition: You are writing an extern block in Rust 2024 edition.
evidence: The unsafe keyword is semantically required to appear before the extern keyword on external blocks.

recipe: Use the wasm_import_module key in the link attribute to specify the WebAssembly module name for extern block items when importing from the host environment; the default module name is env if not specified.
trigger_condition: You are importing symbols from a WebAssembly host environment via an extern block and need to target a specific module.
evidence: The wasm_import_module key may be used to specify the WebAssembly module name for the items within an extern block when importing symbols from the host environment.

recipe: Add the link attribute to an empty extern block to satisfy linking requirements for extern blocks elsewhere in your code, including in upstream crates, instead of modifying each block individually.
trigger_condition: You need to satisfy linking requirements for extern blocks in other parts of your code or in upstream crates without changing each block.
evidence: It is valid to add the link attribute on an empty extern block. You can use this to satisfy the linking requirements of extern blocks elsewhere in your code (including upstream crates) instead of adding the attribute to each extern block.

recipe: The bundle modifier is only compatible with the static linking kind; using it with any other kind will result in a compiler error.
trigger_condition: You are considering using the bundle modifier with a non-static linking kind such as dylib or raw-dylib.
evidence: This modifier is only compatible with the static linking kind. Using any other kind will result in a compiler error.

recipe: When building an rlib or staticlib with +bundle, the native static library is packed into the archive and retrieved during final binary linking.
trigger_condition: You are building an rlib or staticlib and want the native static library embedded in the archive for later retrieval.
evidence: When building a rlib or staticlib +bundle means that the native static library will be packed into the rlib or staticlib archive, and then retrieved from there during linking of the final binary.

recipe: The bundle modifier has no effect when building executables or dynamic libraries, so you can safely include it without changing behavior for those targets.
trigger_condition: You are building an executable or dynamic library target and have bundle modifiers in your link attributes.
evidence: This modifier has no effect when building other targets like executables or dynamic libraries.

recipe: The whole-archive modifier is only compatible with the static linking kind; using it with any other kind will result in a compiler error.
trigger_condition: You are considering using the whole-archive modifier with a non-static linking kind.
evidence: This modifier is only compatible with the static linking kind. Using any other kind will result in a compiler error.

recipe: Use +whole-archive with static linking to link the static library as a whole archive without discarding any object files.
trigger_condition: You need all object files from a static library to be linked, not just those with unresolved symbols.
evidence: +whole-archive means that the static library is linked as a whole archive without throwing any object files away.

recipe: The verbatim modifier is compatible with all linking kinds, so you can apply it regardless of your linking strategy.
trigger_condition: You need to control library name decoration and are unsure if verbatim works with your specific linking kind.
evidence: This modifier is compatible with all linking kinds.

recipe: On Windows, specify kind = "raw-dylib" to have the compiler generate an import library during compilation instead of relying on the linker's normal library resolution logic.
trigger_condition: You are linking against a Windows dynamic library and want the compiler to generate the import library rather than using the linker to find one.
evidence: specifying kind = "raw-dylib" instructs the compiler to generate an import library during compilation and provide that to the linker instead.

recipe: When using raw-dylib on x86 Windows, specify the import_name_type key to control how function names are decorated in the generated import library.
trigger_condition: You are using the raw-dylib link kind on x86 Windows and need to match a specific calling convention decoration format for the generated import library.
evidence: when using the raw-dylib link kind you may also specify the import_name_type key with one of the following values to change how functions are named in the generated import library

recipe: The import_name_type key is only supported on x86 Windows; using it when targeting other platforms will result in a compiler error.
trigger_condition: You are considering using import_name_type on a non-x86-Windows target platform.
evidence: The import_name_type key is only supported on x86 Windows. Using it when targeting other platforms will result in a compiler error.

recipe: Be aware that the import_name_type key has no effect on how variables are named in the generated import library since variables are never decorated.
trigger_condition: You are using import_name_type with raw-dylib and have variable declarations in your extern block.
evidence: Variables are never decorated and so the import_name_type key has no effect on how they are named in the generated import library.

recipe: Apply the link_name attribute to a function or static declaration inside an extern block to specify the exact symbol to import.
trigger_condition: The symbol name in the external library differs from the Rust name you want to use for the declaration.
evidence: The link_name attribute may be applied to declarations inside an extern block to specify the symbol to import for the given function or static.

recipe: Ensure the link_name value is not an empty string and does not contain any NUL bytes (U+0000).
trigger_condition: You are setting the link_name attribute on an extern block declaration.
evidence: The symbol name must not be the empty string or contain any U+0000 (NUL) bytes.

recipe: Only the first link_name attribute on an item has effect; subsequent uses are lints and may become errors in the future.
trigger_condition: You are using multiple link_name attributes on the same extern block item.
evidence: Only the first use of link_name on an item has effect.

recipe: Do not combine the link_name attribute with the link_ordinal attribute on the same item.
trigger_condition: You are trying to use both link_name and link_ordinal on an extern block declaration.
evidence: The link_name attribute may not be used with the link_ordinal attribute.

recipe: The link_name attribute may only be applied to function or static items in an extern block; rustc lints against other positions and it may become an error in the future.
trigger_condition: You are considering applying link_name to something other than a function or static in an extern block.
evidence: The link_name attribute may only be applied to a function or static item in an extern block.

recipe: Use link_ordinal only with raw-dylib linking to specify a stable numeric ordinal for symbol lookup in Windows dynamic libraries.
trigger_condition: You are using raw-dylib on Windows and know the ordinal of a symbol is stable across builds.
evidence: The link_ordinal attribute can be applied on declarations inside an extern block to indicate the numeric ordinal to use when generating the import library to link against.

recipe: Only use link_ordinal when you are certain the ordinal is stable; if not explicitly set in the binary, the assigned ordinal may change between builds.
trigger_condition: You are considering using link_ordinal and the symbol's ordinal might not be explicitly set in the containing binary.
evidence: if the ordinal of a symbol is not explicitly set when its containing binary is built then one will be automatically assigned to it, and that assigned ordinal may change between builds of the binary.

recipe: The link_ordinal attribute is only used with the raw-dylib linking kind; using it with any other kind will result in a compiler error.
trigger_condition: You are considering using link_ordinal with a linking kind other than raw-dylib.
evidence: This attribute is only used with the raw-dylib linking kind. Using any other kind will result in a compiler error.
